panels.figure_caption: The patient at 25 years of age
in_text_mentions: Patient treatment continued with multidisciplinary follow-up (dermatology, psychology and genetics). The same patient has two children which were not affected by the syndrome and are healthy. The patient's parents are phenotypically normal with no consanguinity. Genetic study did not reveal similar cases in the family. Currently at 25 years of age, the patient is periodically monitored and deals with her pathology in a very conscious way, continuing with the treatment for palmoplantar keratoderma (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: 26-year-old proband with GJB6 hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia/Clouston syndrome; panel shows characteristic fingernail dystrophy described in caption and in-text. B: Same Clouston proband; panel shows short thickened toenails, classic nail dystrophy. C: Real patient image of Clouston proband skin with dense follicular hyperkeratotic papules, but no vocabulary finding_key matches this truncal papular hyperkeratosis; palmoplantar keratoderma does not apply to this site/morphology, so excluded per findings-vocabulary rule. D: Oral/teeth close-up with red arrow showing partly absent incisor; no dental finding in allowed vocabulary and teeth are otherwise described as normal, which is expected in hidrotic ED, so no nameable Clouston finding from vocabulary.

The patient had a known history of Clouston syndrome and was born with congenital alopecia (Fig 1, B) and dystrophic nails (Fig 1, C) and later developed palmoplantar keratoderma (Fig 1, A, D).
